title: AppArmor host: privileged containers with a remapped user namespace never restart
body:
### Issue Description

Describe your issueOn an AppArmor host, privileged containers with a remapped user namespace (`--uidmap`/`--gidmap`, or a pod with `--userns` and ID mappings) never restart under `--restart always` or `on-failure` after the main process crashes. Podman emits a `restart` event, but the restart fails and the container stays `Exited`. The same container restarts normally without the user namespace, or with `--security-opt apparmor=unconfined`.

The failing restart is in the `podman container cleanup` process that conmon runs as its exit command. Its error is only visible with `--syslog`:

    level=error msg="Cleaning up container: failed to clean up container <id>: profile \"containers-default-0.66.0\" specified but AppArmor is disabled on the host"

### Steps to reproduce the issue

On Ubuntu 26.04 (AppArmor enabled, rootful podman):

    podman run -d --name rtest-userns --restart always \
      --uidmap 0:200000:65536 --gidmap 0:200000:65536 alpine sleep 4
    podman run -d --name rtest-unconfined --restart always \
      --uidmap 0:200000:65536 --gidmap 0:200000:65536 \
      --security-opt apparmor=unconfined alpine sleep 4
    podman run -d --name rtest-plain --restart always alpine sleep 4
    sleep 20
    for c in rtest-userns rtest-unconfined rtest-plain; do
      podman inspect $c --format "$c: {{.State.Status}} restarts={{.RestartCount}}"
    done


### Describe the results you received

    rtest-userns: exited restarts=1
    rtest-unconfined: running restarts=4
    rtest-plain: running restarts=4

`podman events` for the userns container shows `died`, `restart`, then nothing. `podman start` from a shell starts it without error.


### Describe the results you expected

All three containers keep restarting.

### podman info output

```yaml
host: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, amd64
podman 5.7.0 (Ubuntu package 5.7.0+ds2-3build1, go1.25.0)
conmon 2.1.13, crun 1.21 (+APPARMOR +SELINUX +SECCOMP)
containers-common 0.66.0 (golang-github-containers-common 0.66.0+ds2-3)
AppArmor parser 5.0.2; AppArmorEnabled=true, SELinux=false, seccomp=true
cgroups v2, cgroup manager systemd, netavark, overlay, sqlite db
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Privileged

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

AppArmor active (`/sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled` = `Y`, securityfs mounted on the host)

Reproduced on both 5.7.0 (Ubuntu package) and 6.1.3 (latest upstream release, built from the tag); the error in 6.1.3 names `containers-default-0.69.2`.

### Additional information

Also reproduced with upstream v6.1.3 built from the release tag (make podman, default BUILDTAGS incl. apparmor seccomp systemd), same host, conmon 2.1.13, crun 1.21.

comments.body:
Same on Debian 13.7 (kernel 6.12.111, AppArmor enabled) with Debian's podman 5.4.2, crun 1.21, conmon 2.1.12, containers-common 0.62.2, all rootful. So it's not specific to Ubuntu's userns restrictions, and it predates 5.7. Your three containers after 25 s:

```
rtest-userns:     exited  restarts=1  apparmor=containers-default-0.62.2
rtest-unconfined: running restarts=5  apparmor=unconfined
rtest-plain:      running restarts=5  apparmor=containers-default-0.62.2
```

Events `create init start died restart`, then nothing; `podman start` from a shell works. `--restart on-failure:3` with a command that exits 1 stops at `restarts=1` the same way. With `podman --syslog run` the cleanup logs `profile "containers-default-0.62.2" specified but AppArmor is disabled on the host` from `podman ... --syslog container cleanup --stopped-only <id>`.

One thing that may save someone time: it doesn't look like the cleanup is being treated as rootless. With `strace -f -p <conmon pid> -e trace=execve,unshare,setns -v` across the exit, the cleanup podman ran as root, in the host user namespace, with no `_CONTAINERS_USERNS_CONFIGURED` (or any userns variable) in its environment, and it neither re-executed itself nor called `unshare`. conmon's `CapEff` was `000001ffffffffff` for both the mapped and the plain container. So of the three checks in `IsSupported()` (v0.62.2), it would be the `runcaa.IsEnabled()` or the `apparmor_parser` lookup failing in that path, not `IsRootless()`; I didn't pin down which.

Workaround that keeps the profile: a Quadlet unit with `UIDMap=`/`GIDMap=` and `[Service] Restart=always` was restarted 4 times in 25 s with no AppArmor error, since it runs `--rm` without `--restart` and systemd does the restarting.

Write-up: https://homelabpostmortem.com/2026/10/11/rootful-podman-restarts-a-uidmap-container-once-on-an-apparmor-host/
